extracted.intended_audience: school/college/university administrators, Title IX coordinators, and policy drafters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and operating a recipient's Title IX grievance procedures, including required disclosures, standards, appeals, supportive measures, and protections. Focused on what recipients must include in policies and how they must apply them in formal complaints of sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe or list disciplinary sanctions and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must either “describe the range of” or “list the possible” disciplinary sanctions and remedies that could result from a determination that a respondent is responsible for Title IX sexual harassment (§106.45(b)(1)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to increase transparency and predictability of the grievance process but is not intended to be exclusive or to unnecessarily restrict a recipient's ability to tailor sanctions to specific situations. Recipients are not required to state the factors that might be considered in deciding sanctions; they may choose to describe a range or list specific possible sanctions. The list/range not being exclusive means recipients retain flexibility to impose appropriate sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and apply a consistent standard of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients' grievance processes must state up front whether the standard of evidence to determine responsibility is the preponderance of the evidence or the clear and convincing evidence standard, and must apply the same standard to all formal complaints (students and employees) (§106.45(b)(1)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selected standard must be chosen, stated, and applied consistently by each recipient to all formal complaints of sexual harassment. This consistency is required to ensure fairness and avoid arbitrary or inconsistent decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify procedures and permissible bases for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include in their grievance process the permissible bases and procedures for appeals and must offer appeals equally to both parties on at least three bases: (1) procedural irregularity that affected the outcome; (2) new evidence not reasonably available when the determination was made that could affect the outcome; and (3) conflict of interest or bias by the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker (§106.45(b)(1)(viii) and §106.45(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are mandatory and must be available equally to complainants and respondents. Parties may raise procedural defects during a live hearing without waiting to file an appeal, and may still appeal on the basis of procedural irregularity after a determination. The Title IX Coordinator is tasked with effective implementation of remedies so complainants should not need to appeal simply to challenge remedy implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe range of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients' grievance procedures must describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents (§106.45(b)(1)(ix)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement is to describe the range (not an exhaustive list) of individualized services that may be available. Recipients are required to offer supportive measures to complainants and engage in an interactive discussion about the complainant's wishes; there is no analogous obligation to offer supportive measures to respondents, though the regulations define supportive measures to incentivize availability to respondents where appropriate. Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party. Recipients may, but are not required to, publish names/contact information of external community resources; community resource lists may change frequently, so describing types of measures is sufficient. A non-exhaustive list of examples appears in the definition of “supportive measures” in §106.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect legally recognized privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure that information protected by a legally recognized privilege (e.g., attorney-client, doctor-patient, spousal) is not used during the grievance process (§106.45(b)(1)(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision was added to ensure a recipient's grievance process respects legally recognized privileges and prevents compelled disclosure of privileged communications during the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide written notice of allegations (including complainant identity and sufficient details)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a formal complaint, recipients must provide written notice of the allegations to both parties equally, which includes the identity of the complainant and sufficient details about the alleged incident (§106.45(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice benefits both parties by allowing preparation and avoids surprise interviews that can lead to unfair reliance on uncertain recollection. The Department determined a grievance process cannot proceed with fundamental fairness without apprising the respondent of the complainant's identity and sufficient details once a formal complaint initiates the grievance process. Recipients must also offer supportive measures at or after notice and must keep their provision confidential to the extent possible to protect complainant safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit retaliation for exercising Title IX rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations add §106.71 prohibiting any person from intimidating, threatening, coercing, or discriminating against any individual for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX, including making a report or formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may communicate this protection in any manner they choose. Complaints of retaliation may be filed with the recipient and handled under the recipient's “prompt and equitable” grievance procedures for non-sexual harassment sex discrimination complaints. §106.71 protects all parties, witnesses, and others from retaliation. Recipients must keep provision of supportive measures confidential to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning against false statements (conditional on recipient code)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice may include information about any prohibition in the recipient's own code of conduct against knowingly submitting false information during a disciplinary proceeding, but only if the recipient's code of conduct contains such a prohibition (§106.45(b)(2)(i)(B) and related discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recipient's code addresses false statements, both parties deserve to know how the school treats false statements (the warning applies equally to complainants and respondents). The Department cautions that a finding of not responsible alone cannot be the sole basis to conclude a party made a bad faith, materially false statement; any disciplinary action for false statements must be fact-specific and not based solely on the outcome of the Title IX determination. The Department declines to mandate that recipients adopt sanctions for false statements or prescribe minimum consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process independence from criminal investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: A §106.45 grievance process occurs independently of any concurrent criminal investigation; recipients are obligated to inform parties of the allegations as part of their grievance process and are not required to adopt law-enforcement investigative best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While commenters argued for delayed notice to preserve criminal-investigative integrity (e.g., unplanned interviews), the Department reiterates that educational institutions are not law enforcement and the grievance process's notice obligation is a necessary procedural benefit. The Department does not require recipients to adopt law enforcement standards; overlapping investigations must be managed consistent with the recipient's obligations, and recipients may consider temporary law-enforcement requests in context (other sections of the regulations address coordination/delays). The grievance process's obligation to provide notice is intended to ensure due process and fairness for parties in the educational context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibility for implementation of remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for effective implementation of remedies (§106.45(b)(7)(iv) as discussed in appeals section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Title IX Coordinator is charged with implementing remedies, complainants should not need to use appeals procedures merely to challenge remedy selection or implementation. This clarifies who is responsible for remedy effectiveness and assists complainants in obtaining relief without unnecessary appeals.
